title: pkix-path cannot parse a pre-1970 UTCTime, so PKITS 4.2.3 has no verdict
description:
PKITS 4.2.3 'Valid pre2000 UTC notBefore Date Test3' ships Validpre2000UTCnotBeforeDateTest3EE.crt with

  notBefore = 500101120100Z

which RFC 5280 §4.1.2.5.1 reads as 1 Jan 1950 (UTCTime YY >= 50 means 19YY). The der crate's UtcTime supports 1970-2049, so the certificate does not parse at all: pkix-path returns a load error rather than a verdict, and the vector cannot be scored against NIST ground truth. NIST says it is valid.

openssl parses it fine (openssl x509 -dates reports notBefore=Jan 1 12:01:00 1950 GMT), so this is a floor in our DER layer, not a malformed certificate.

This workspace supports 1970-2049 and does not fork der, which is a standing decision, so this is recorded as a deliberate limitation rather than a defect. It is listed in known_gaps() in pkix-difftest/tests/pkits_ground_truth.rs, which fails if it ever starts passing.

The options, if it is ever worth closing:

1. Leave it. A 1950 notBefore is only reachable from a certificate issued under a profile nobody should be using, and the failure direction is safe -- an unparseable certificate is refused, not accepted.
2. Pre-process the validity field before handing the certificate to der, rewriting a pre-1970 UTCTime to the 1970 floor. Cheap, but it means pkix-path validates a certificate whose bytes it altered, and the altered field is one the signature covers.
3. Carry our own UTCTime decoder for the validity field only. No der fork, but it duplicates a parser that is exactly the kind of code this workspace prefers not to own.

Only the 1970 floor is at issue here; the 2049 ceiling is RFC 5280's own rule (§4.1.2.5 requires GeneralizedTime for 2050 and later) and is correct as it stands.
